To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the shape of an animal depends on the shape of its connective tissue extracelluar matrices (ECMs) and that ECM shapes depend on holding collagen fibrils together with elastic glycan strings, called shape modules.
cartilage is held together, and is able to resist compressive and tensive stresses, by elastic PG shape modules.
the ECMs that hold us together, are based on shape modules that contain repeating AGAG strings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
shape modules in ECMs and their role in determining ECM shapes.
the role of shape modules in the ECMs of tissues and the pathological changes that occur when they are disrupted.
the structure and function of shape modules in ECMs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the shapes of animals are determined by the shapes of the elastic shape modules of their ECMs, which are held together by elastic strings of AGAGs.

the shapes and mechanical properties of animal ECMs depend on the regular, frequent and specific interactions of AGAG chains, and that the shapes and responses of cartilage ECMs depend on these and the presence of aggrecan and its associated water.
the shapes of animals are maintained by shape modules, which are elastic glycan strings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cartilage shape and function depend on elastic glycan strings, and that their degradation leads to osteoarthrosis.
shape modules are the basis of all ECMs and that their degradation leads to loss of tissue integrity.
shape modules hold us together, and are held together.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ECMs are not just scaffolds but also elastic, active components in the maintenance of shape.
the shape of the animal is determined by elastic shape modules.
ECMs are based on shape modules, held together by elastic AGAG strings, which are the basis of their anisotropic responses to mechanical stress.
